reconcile.connective: Commentators read the two counts by location: many of the 500 who saw the risen Christ in Galilee never traveled to the Jerusalem vigil.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells's Skeptic's Annotated Bible lists the two totals as contradictory answers to the same question, without the Galilee/Jerusalem split harmonizers propose.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.work: The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "How many believers were there at the time of the ascension?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/believers.html)
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (online; contra/believers.html)

excerpts.excerpt_text: the number . . . about an hundred and twenty--Many, therefore, of the "five hundred brethren" who saw their risen Lord "at once" (Co1 15:6), must have remained in Galilee.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly bridges both verses: reads Acts 1:15's 120 as the Jerusalem remnant while explicitly citing 1 Cor 15:6's '500 brethren at once' and locating that appearance in Galilee, explaining the numeric gap as geography rather than a headcount error.

pd_work.resource: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown, Commentary Critical and Explanatory on the Whole Bible (1871), on Acts 1:15
pd_work.author: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown
pd_work.note: JFB's own note on Acts 1:15 (already the reconcile pole's excerpt) is the harmonizing treatment of this exact numeric pair. Haley's An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874) does not treat this passage — confirmed by a full-text search of the archive.org OCR text for 'hundred and twenty,' 'five hundred brethren,' 'Acts i. 15,' and '1 Cor. xv. 6,' all zero hits.
